data.narrative:
Duranium is a pre-seed stage Climate & Energy company founded by Berkley Noble and Brenden Prins-McKinney. The company has raised $2M to date. The Climate & Energy sector includes a broad peer universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable (LNZA), though stage-specific comparables at the pre-seed level are limited.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable and forms the analytical foundation. Using the $2M total raised as a valuation proxy, application of a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for pre-seed to next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $5M. Peer-median analysis is not applicable given insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables in the narrow peer set; while 9 same-sector companies exist (including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen), none meet the filtering criteria of 3+ datapoints at matching stage or valuation tier.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $4M to $6M, with a median point of $5M. This range reflects the limited methodological basis—only one applicable approach—and the scarcity of pre-seed stage comparables in the sector. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct peer valuation anchors, the applicability of the 2.5x multiplier to this specific company's risk profile and market conditions, and the early-stage nature of the enterprise. Additional data on similar-stage climate tech fundings would strengthen conviction in this range.
